'''Jaren Jackson Jr.''' (born September 15, 1999) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. He is currently projected to be a Top 5 pick for the [[2018 NBA draft]], with [[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] labeling him as the most complete college big man of the competition that year.<ref>https://www.theringer.com/nba/2018/2/6/16976438/jaren-jackson-jr-best-big-man-draft</ref>

==High school career==
Jackson started his high school career with [[Park Tudor School|Park Tudor school]]. He played varsity for three years, where he averaged 10 points a game, 6 rebounds a game, and 3 blocks a game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/jaren-jackson/543Mzlz0EeOzMAAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|title=Jaren Jackson's High School Basketball Stats|website=MaxPreps.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> Jackson won two [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] state basketball championships while at Park Tudor.<ref>{{cite web|title=Class 2A: Park Tudor wins 4th title in 5 years|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/03/28/class-park-tudor-repeats-win-frankton/70597226/|website=Indystar.com|publisher=Indy Star|accessdate=2017-12-30}}</ref> Jackson was teammates with current [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier University]] standout [[Trevon Bluiett]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Park Tudor: 84 Westview:57|url=http://wishtv.com/2014/03/29/park-tudor-84-westview-57/|publisher=Wish TV|accessdate=2017-12-30}}</ref>He then transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] for his senior year,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.verbalcommits.com/players/jaren-jackson-jr|title=Verbal Commits {{!}} Jaren Jackson, Jr. Player Profile, Highlights, Offers, Twitter|website=www.verbalcommits.com|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> where he started for their varsity squad.

=== Recruiting ===
Jackson was considered one of the top players in the 2017 graduating class.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/jaren-jackson-jr|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. {{!}} NBADraft.net|website=www.nbadraft.net|language=en|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> Scout.com ranked Jackson the 5th best player nationally,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/193446-jaren-jackson|title=Jaren Jackson, La Lumiere School PF - Scout|website=www.scout.com|language=en|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> 1st in his respective position, and 2nd overall in the midwest region. 247 Sports ranked him 7th nationally,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jaren-Jackson-78413|title=Jaren Jackson, La Lumiere School , Power Forward|website=247Sports|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> being 4th in his position. ESPN ranked him 8th in the ESPN 100,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/207895/jaren-jackson|title=Jaren Jackson - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-01-18}}</ref> being 2nd in his position and 2nd regionally.

==College career==
On September 15, 2016, Jaren Jackson Jr. announced his intentions to sign a letter of intent to go to Michigan State. He signed the [[letter of intent]] on November 9, 2016.<ref name=":0" /> Jackson would make his collegiate debut on November 10, 2017, recording 13 points and a season-high 13 rebounds in a blowout 98–66 win over the [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida Ospreys]]. Four days later, he would record a then-season-high 19 points in an 88–81 loss to the #1 ranked [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. On December 5, Jackson would put up 11 points and a career-high 8 blocks in a 62–52 win over the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. Four days later, he would record 17 points and another career-high 13 rebounds in a blowout 88–63 win over the [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds men's basketball|Southern Utah Thunderbirds]]. On January 22, 2018, Jackson recorded a then-season-high 21 points to go with 11 rebounds and 6 blocks in an 87–74 win over [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. On February 13, he would put up a career-high 27 points in a blowout 87–57 win over the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. At the end of the regular season for Michigan State, Jackson would be named both the Big Ten's Defensive Player of the Year and Freshman of the Year, as well as be named to the Big Ten's All-Freshman Team and the All-Big Ten's Third Team. On April 2, Jackson would declare his entry into the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he's considered a potential top-tier lottery selection.

== National team career ==
Jackson helped the United States of America's under-17 basketball team win the gold medal at the FIBA 2016 World Championships. Jackson scored two points and had six rebounds in the gold medal game. He averaged 4.3 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.2 blocked shots, and shot 53 percent from the field.<ref name=":0" /> He was a member of the USA Junior National Select Team that participated in the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]]. Coming off the bench, Jackson tallied 13 points and a game-high nine rebounds in 25 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|title=LiveStats - USA vs World Select Team - Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=2017-04-08|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jackson is the son of former professional basketball coach and former NBA player [[Jaren Jackson]].
